US Imposes Tariffs on Swedish Gas & Water Utilities Products, Straining Industry Operations

The United States has implemented a 25% tariff on all gas metering devices, water purification equipment, and pipeline components exported from Sweden’s Gas & Water Utilities industry, in a move that industry observers say is already reverberating through Sweden’s utilities sector. The tariffs, introduced last month and effective immediately, cover a range of products that account for a significant portion of Sweden’s annual global exports in the sector, valued at approximately SEK 3.5 billion ($320 million), with the US historically representing nearly a quarter of the export market.

Industry trade group Svenska Gas och Vattenförbundet (SGV) reports that several firms have begun scaling back shifts at production sites in Norrköping and Sundsvall in response to rapidly declining US orders. “Our members are seeing order volumes from US partners drop by as much as 60% in the last three weeks,” said SGV chair Lena Sjöberg. “This has forced companies to consider temporary layoffs and to review operational capacity.”

At Nordiska Utilities AB, a leading producer of water filtration systems, CEO Mikael Lindholm confirmed the company has reduced overtime and postponed plans to expand its facilities. “We are currently reassessing our US market strategy and shifting focus to other regions, but it’s clear this situation places local jobs under pressure,” Lindholm stated.

Union representatives voiced concerns about the uncertainty facing workers. “Our members are worried about their futures. While companies are trying to avoid redundancies, we have already seen a freeze on new hires and reduced hours at several sites,” said Elin Kallström, spokesperson for the Swedish Utilities Workers Union.

According to industry analysts, if the tariffs remain in place, more pronounced effects such as permanent job cuts and site consolidations may follow. The Ministry for Foreign Trade has stated it is in ongoing discussions with US counterparts and is “committed to supporting Swedish utilities exporters through this challenging period.”
